pages.title: A Beautiful Voice
pages.content:
It is Friday. Yusuf and Grandpa are together at home. Then they hear the adhan from the mosque. Yusuf listens. “Grandpa, who gives the first adhan?” he asks. Grandpa smiles. “His name is Bilal. He has got a very beautiful voice. Listen to his story, my boy.” “Great! I love stories!” Yusuf says.

“Bilal lives in Mecca a long time ago,” Grandpa says. “He is a slave. His mother is a slave, too. Bilal works for a rich man. The man’s name is Umayya. Bilal works all day. He looks after the camels in the hot sun. It is very difficult.”

vocabulary.definition: The call to prayer from the mosque.
The sound of a person when they talk or sing.
A person who works for another person and is not free.

pages.title: Life in Old Mecca
pages.content:
“Is Umayya a good man, Grandpa?” Yusuf asks.

“No, Yusuf,” Grandpa says. “He is not kind to Bilal. In Mecca, many people pray to idols. Umayya loves his idols, too. Life in Mecca is not fair. Some people are very rich. They have got a lot of gold. They eat from gold plates. But many people are poor. They are hungry. Some people say, ‘Bilal is a slave. He is not important.’ Bilal is very sad.”

vocabulary.definition: Things of stone or wood. Some people pray to them.

pages.title: Allah Is One
pages.content:
Yusuf is sad, too. “Poor Bilal!” he says.

“But one day, Bilal hears some news,” Grandpa says. “There is a new Prophet in Mecca. His name is Muhammad (pbuh). He tells people about Allah. Allah is One. Do not pray to idols. All people are equal. Bilal thinks about this for many days. One night, he goes to Abu Bakr’s house. Abu Bakr is a friend of the Prophet (pbuh). He tells Bilal about Islam. Bilal believes in Allah. He is a Muslim now!”

pages.title: A Hot Rock
pages.content:
“Is Umayya happy, Grandpa?” Yusuf asks.

“No, he is very angry,” Grandpa says. “He takes Bilal out in the hot sun. He puts a big, hot rock on Bilal. ‘Pray to our idols!’ he shouts. But Bilal only says, ‘One, One. Allah is One.’ Bilal is in a lot of pain, but his heart is very strong. Then Abu Bakr comes. He gives Umayya some gold. He takes the rock off Bilal. ‘You are free now, Bilal,’ he says. Bilal is very happy. He thanks Allah.”

pages.title: A New City
pages.content:
Yusuf smiles. “Bilal is free!” he says. “Where does he go?”

“Later, the Muslims go to a new city,” Grandpa says. “Its name is Medina. They build a mosque there. It is time to pray. The Prophet (pbuh) wants a man for the adhan. Who is it? It is Bilal! His voice is very beautiful. And he is never afraid. Bilal goes up on a high roof. People are quiet. Everybody waits.”

pages.title: The First Adhan
pages.content:
Yusuf sits up. “What does Bilal say?” he asks.

“Bilal says, ‘Allahu akbar! Allah is the greatest!’” Grandpa says. “People hear his voice. They come to the mosque. They pray together. Rich people and poor people stand side by side. Bilal is not a slave now. He is a friend of the Prophet (pbuh). All people are equal. Only a good heart makes a person better.”

Then they hear the adhan again. Yusuf stands up. “Grandpa, let’s go to the mosque!” he says. Grandpa takes his hand. They walk to the mosque together.
